root_cause: prvAllowIPPacketIPv4() and prvAllowIPPacketIPv6() skipped the IP header checksum and the protocol checksum (whose checker also enforces minimum protocol sizes) for any frame whose Ethernet source MAC matched one of the device's own endpoints, a loopback exemption that any sender on the link can claim by setting that MAC.
notes: Advisory: affected V4.0.0 to V4.2.5 and V4.3.0 to V4.4.0, patched in V4.2.6 and V4.4.1; the repository History.txt lists the change under V4.4.0, so fixed_ref follows the advisory. PR #1335 bundles seven separate fixes; only commit fc68874 (Remove MAC-based loopback validation bypass) belongs to this sample. The exemption was meant for loopback frames; the attacker must be on the same link (adjacent).

component: Zephyr Bluetooth host, encryption change handling
root_cause: hci_encrypt_change() treated an HCI Encryption Change event with status SUCCESS as a completed security change and ran the security update and upper-layer success paths even when the event's encrypt flag showed no change, so a peripheral that rejected encryption with error code 0 left L2CAP, ATT, SMP and applications assuming an encrypted link; the fix drops events that do not change conn->encrypt.
notes: Zephyr merges by rebase: the PR branch commit 632e43178c33fbe1d27be033557f49b2089bb8d5 landed on main as bf363d7; vulnerable_ref is its parent on main. Backports: PR 74124 (v3.6), 74123 (v3.5), 74122 (v2.7). The trigger is a peripheral that answers an encryption request with a reject carrying error code 0, which the Core Specification forbids. The effects are in other host files (conn.c, l2cap.c, att.c, smp.c), so the audit scope is the whole host directory.

root_cause: _isr_wrapper in arch/riscv/core/isr.S did not reload gp with the kernel's __global_pointer$ on exception or system call entry from user mode, so kernel code that addresses globals relative to gp ran with a value set by an untrusted user thread.
notes: Only builds with CONFIG_RISCV_GP=y and user mode threads (CONFIG_USERSPACE) are affected. Commit 6193a93 (reset global pointer on exception) is the PR-branch hash; Zephyr rebased the three PR commits onto main, and 408c151 is the merged tip on main (it contains the fix); the main-branch hash of the fix commit itself was not identified. vulnerable_ref v3.7.0 follows the advisory (versions up to and including 3.7). v3.7 backport: PR 81370. The fix was read from the PR files view, not from a raw diff.

root_cause: pl011_irq_tx_enable() emulated the TX-ready interrupt by calling the application's TX callback in a loop while PL011_IMSC_TXIM was set, assuming the FIFO would drain; with CTS hardware flow control and the peer holding CTS inactive the FIFO never drains, so the loop never ends and the calling thread hangs.
notes: Advisory: affected >= 4.1.0 and < 4.3.1, and >= 4.4.0 and < 4.4.2. Needs CTS hardware flow control enabled; the attacker is the wired serial peer. The diff was read on the PR-branch commit d5972f62021b40397dbec25de67783fe8735d4d1; the single-commit PR landed on main as 68e7022. Backports: PR 110768 (v4.4), 110767 (v4.3). The audit scope is the driver file because drivers/serial holds many unrelated drivers.

root_cause: __net_defragment() in net/net.c did not require a fragment's IP total length to be at least header + 8 bytes before computing len = ip_len - IP_HDR_SIZE and placing the new in-band hole descriptor at thisfrag + len / 8, so a payload of 0 to 7 bytes put the new descriptor on top of the fragment's own data and the following memcpy() overwrote the hole-list metadata.
notes: Only builds with CONFIG_IP_DEFRAG. The same commit (add IP_MIN_FRAG_DATAGRAM_SIZE and reject shorter datagrams) also fixes CVE-2022-30552, where ip_len below 20 makes len underflow; that is not a separate sample. The skill reaches the underflow half through the subtraction question, but not the 21 to 27 byte case, which needs the in-band hole descriptor to be seen. Search results show later (2026) U-Boot list patches touching the same reassembly code; they were not examined.

root_cause: The input profile's classic_bonded_only option (ClassicBondedOnly in input.conf) defaulted to false in profiles/input/device.c, so hidp_add_connection() accepted HID connections and keyboard reports from Classic devices that were not bonded, against the HID requirement for Security Mode 4.
notes: The GitHub repository is a mirror of bluez.git on git.kernel.org. The option already existed (added for an earlier issue) with default false; the fix only flips the default and the comment in input.conf. Uses of classic_bonded_only were read at tag 5.70. Distributions can override the value in /etc/bluetooth/input.conf.

root_cause: _iphc_encode() sized the dispatch buffer by assuming that a snippet of undefined type after the IPv6 header is always an 8-byte UDP header, while the compression pass chose what to write from the IPv6 next-header field, so IPv6 extension headers in that snippet were written past the buffer.
notes: Advisory: all versions before 2022.10; master fix 4a081f8, 2022.10 branch fix dafc397. OSV lists an unrelated merge commit (365fbed, an ESP32 I2C change) as the fix; ignore it. The frame travels the forwarding or sending path that re-encodes IPHC.

component: Contiki-NG RPL hop-by-hop option (RPL-Lite and RPL-Classic)
root_cause: rpl_ext_header_hbh_update() read 16-bit fields of the RPL option through a struct pointer at an offset set by the sender's padding, without checking the 2n alignment RFC 6553 requires, so an odd offset caused an unaligned access that can fault on strict-alignment MCUs.
notes: Advisory: Contiki-NG 4.9 and earlier. vulnerable_ref is the parent of the first fix commit (1986282, RPL-Classic); the second (8c3d507, RPL-Lite) is fixed_ref; PR merged into develop on 2024-09-25. Impact depends on the CPU: strict-alignment cores fault, others only read slowly.

root_cause: bootutil_img_validate() accepted any TLV type from the unprotected (unsigned) TLV area, so dependency and boot-record entries that later steps trust could be added without breaking the image signature; the fix allows only signature, key, hash and encryption entries there.
notes: Fix is two commits: ea1cdfd adds bootutil_tlv_iter_is_prot() in tlv.c, da2e2ab adds the allow list of unprotected TLV types in image_validate.c; vulnerable_ref is the parent of ea1cdfd. The release notes put the fix under version 2.1.0, while the advisory text says versions below 1.11.0 are affected. The check can be turned off (ALLOW_ROGUE_TLVS, later renamed MCUBOOT_USE_TLV_ALLOW_LIST with reversed logic). Where the dependency and boot-record TLVs are consumed was not traced.

root_cause: The server kept root privileges after user authentication and switched to the user only when it forked the session shell, so channel requests handled in between, notably unix socket forwarding (newstreamlocal() in src/svr-tcpfwd.c), connected to local sockets as root, bypassing file permissions and SO_PEERCRED checks; the fix drops privileges right after authentication.
notes: Affected 2024.84 to 2025.88 (unix socket forwarding arrived in 2024.84). The fix is a design change spread over several files (PR 391 adds svr_switch_user() and DROPBEAR_SVR_DROP_PRIVS; PR 394 restores seteuid for reading authorized_keys); 2025.89 also refuses unix stream forwarding under a forced command. newstreamlocal() was confirmed in src/svr-tcpfwd.c at DROPBEAR_2025.88; the diff of the forwarding path itself was not read. Default OpenWrt (root as the only SSH user) is not exploitable.
